original_question: Let f(z_1, z_2) be a polynomial that does not vanish in the bidisk D^2. Is the optimal polynomial approximant of 1/f in H^2(D^2) zero-free in D^2?
target_in_paper: Section 4.2, Open Question 4 ([Weak Shanks Conjecture]), the open problem asking whether Hardy-space optimal polynomial approximants to 1/f on the bidisk remain zero-free when f is a polynomial with no zeros in D^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
correct_elements: Your draft already has the right ambient space H^2(D^2), the right class of functions f (two-variable polynomials nonvanishing on D^2), and the right zero-set question for approximants to 1/f. That is exactly the weak Shanks problem singled out in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
missing_details: The paper's several-variable setup is over complex polynomials, i.e. f should be taken in C[z1,z2], with D^2 the open unit bidisk in C^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))

In the bidisk case one must first fix an ordering of the monomials before defining optimal polynomial approximants; the paper explicitly notes this and gives degree lexicographic order as an example. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))

What is defined is an n-th optimal polynomial approximant p_n, not a single unrestricted best approximant; the question concerns the family of finite-dimensional minimizers. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))

A fully stand-alone version should define the finite-dimensional spaces P_n coming from the chosen ordering and say that p_n minimizes ||pf-1||_{H^2(D^2)} over p in P_n. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
The quantifier should be explicit: the intended question is whether every p_n, for each n >= 0, is zero-free in D^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
Zero-free should be spelled out as having no zeros anywhere in the open bidisk D^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
refined_question: Fix the open unit bidisk D^2 = {(z1,z2) in C^2 : |z1| < 1, |z2| < 1} and the Hardy space H^2(D^2). After fixing an ordering of the monomials in z1 and z2 (for example, degree lexicographic order), let P_n be the span of the first n+1 monomials in that order, and for a polynomial f in C[z1,z2] satisfying f(z1,z2) != 0 on D^2, let p_n be the n-th optimal polynomial approximant to 1/f, i.e. the polynomial p_n in P_n that minimizes ||p f - 1||_{H^2(D^2)} over p in P_n. Is it true that for every n >= 0, the polynomial p_n is zero-free in D^2? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
justification: Section 4.2 is the relevant target because it introduces the bidisk setting, explains that multivariable opas require a fixed ordering of monomials, and then states Open Question 4 under the label Weak Shanks Conjecture. Your draft captures the core hypothesis and conclusion almost verbatim, but it is not fully paper-faithful as a stand-alone question because it suppresses the indexing by n, the dependence on a chosen monomial ordering, and the precise finite-dimensional minimization that defines the approximants. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2102.01725))
